l1_text:
## tsa03-p01
When that light-natured Śiva-reality stated cannot be entered in the unbroken circle, then, seeing autonomy-power itself as preponderant, one experiences undivided Bhairava-immersion. And his teaching is this: all this host of things is mere reflection in the sky of awareness, since endowed with reflection-marks. For this is the mark of reflection: what, shining dividedly, unable, shines only as unmixed with other — that is reflection — like face-form in a mirror, like taste in tooth-water, like smell in the nose, like couple's touch in the bliss-sense, like thorn-spear touch in the inner touch-sense, like echo in the sky. (3.1) For that taste is not primary — since no unseen effect like disease-cure is seen. (3.2) Nor are smell and touch primary for the qualified — since in their absence there is no yoga, and since no effect-series begins. (3.3) Nor are they non-existent — from seeing body-dusting, emission, and the rest. (3.4) Sound too is not primary — from hearing like an approaching echo that someone speaks. (3.5) Thus, as this reflected shines, so too the universe is in the Lord's light. (3.6) "But here what would be the source-image? Let there be none!" (3.7) "But is it causeless? Ah — then the cause-question: what, by source-word logic? The cause is the Lord's power itself, non-different from autonomy, shall be — and since bearing the universe-reflection, hence the Lord's universe-bodiedness: for the universe is consciousness-made, the manifest station of awareness — hence that very universe here is counter-image, hence its reflection-bearing. And that, so far, the Lord's universe-bodiedness is nature — not ungrasped, since graspinglessness of consciousness-nature is impossible. (3.8) For in non-grasping of own nature there would be inertness itself, in truth. And this grasping is not conventional, but unavoidably following mere consciousness-nature — declared pregnant with supreme resonance; and it grasps as much as is the Lord's power-multitude ordering the universe. (3.9) Therein, chief are three powers of the Lord: unsurpassed, will, unfolding — that itself is the grasping-triad a, i, u. From this triad alone the whole power-expanse is enacted. In the unsurpassed itself is rest, bliss; in will itself is rest, sovereignty; in unfolding itself is rest, wave, the beginning of action-power. That itself is the grasping-triad ā, ī, ū. (3.10) Therein, the earlier grasping-triad, since essence is light-portion, is sun-natured; the latter grasping-triad, since rest-nature-bliss-preponderant, is moon-natured — so far as there is no entry of action-portion. (3.11) But when action enters into will and sovereignty — what is called wished and willed — then its two divisions: by light alone, ra-sound; by rest, la-sound — since ra and la are light-pillar-natured. And the wished is not manifest like outer; if manifest-formed, that itself would be creation, not will or sovereignty. Hence from unmanifestness alone is mere sound of ra and la — no standing like consonant. (3.12) That four-phoneme set, since bearing both shadows, is neuter — ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, ḹ. (3.13)"

## tsa03-p01 — seeing: everything as reflection
Can't enter the unbroken circle? Then look at the power that won't be broken: autonomy itself — and rest in Bhairava-immersion without a ripple of thought. The teaching is one sentence: everything you see is a reflection in the sky of knowing. A reflection has a mark: it shows up split off, helpless — unable to stand apart from what it shines in. A face in a mirror. Taste on teeth in water. Smell in a nose. Lovers' touch. A thorn's touch felt inwardly. An echo in the sky. None of these run the show — taste cures no disease — yet none are nothing either: dust the body and something lifts; seed flows. The universe stands to the Lord's light exactly so. "But where's the original the world reflects?" — there needn't be one. "Then is it causeless?" — no: its cause is the Lord's own power, which just is autonomy, holding the world's reflection and so bodied as the world. And this world-bodiedness isn't ungrasped — a consciousness that never grasped itself would be inert matter. The grasping isn't a label stuck on; it comes with being conscious the way resonance comes with a bell, and it reaches exactly as far as the Lord's powers order the world. Three of those powers are chief: the Unsurpassed, Will, Unfolding — grasped as a-i-u. From that one triad the whole power-pageant is performed. Rest in the Unsurpassed is bliss; rest in Will is sovereignty; rest in Unfolding is the wave where action-power begins — grasped as ā-ī-ū. The first triad is sun, being mostly light; the second is moon, being mostly restful bliss — until action walks in. When action enters willing and commanding — the wished, the willed — it splits in two: by sheer light, the sound ra; by rest, the sound la (both are pillars of light). The wished stays unmanifest — flaunted, it would be a made thing, not willing. So ra and la are bare sounds, never full consonants. With both lights and shadows in them, the four — ṛ ṝ ḷ ḹ — are neuter.

c1.body:
When the unbroken circle cannot be entered, the seer rests in autonomy-power and experiences undivided Bhairava-immersion. The teaching: all things are mere reflections in the sky of awareness — mirror, taste, smell, touch, echo. Reflections are non-primary (no unseen effects) yet not non-existent. The universe stands to the Lord's light the same way. The "no source-image?" objection is dissolved: the cause is the Lord's power = autonomy, which holds the universe's reflection; graspinglessness would be inertness. Grasping is non-conventional, resonance-pregnant, coextensive with the power-multitude. Three chief powers (unsurpassed/will/unfolding) = grasping-triads a-i-u / ā-ī-ū; whole power-expanse enacted thence. Sun-triad (light-portion) vs moon-triad (rest-bliss) while action absent; action entering will/sovereignty → ra/la sounds (light-pillar), unmanifest (else creation, not will). Four neuters ṛṝḷḹ bearing both shadows.

The passage moves in four steps, each deepening the seeing. First, the reflection doctrine: all things = mere reflections in awareness-sky (six similes: mirror, taste in tooth-water, smell in nose, couple's touch, thorn-spear touch, echo in sky); reflections are non-primary (no unseen effects like disease-cure) yet not non-existent (body-dusting, emission are seen); the universe stands to the Lord's light exactly so. Second, the "no source-image?" objection dissolved: cause = Lord's power = autonomy (graspinglessness → inertness; grasping non-conventional, resonance-pregnant, coextensive with power-multitude). The grasping is not a label stuck on; it comes with being conscious the way resonance comes with a bell. Third, three chief powers = anuttara/icchā/unmeṣa = grasping-triads a-i-u / ā-ī-ū; whole power-expanse enacted thence; sun-triad (light-portion, sūryātmaka) vs moon-triad (rest-bliss, somātmaka) while action absent. Fourth, action entering will/sovereignty → ra/la sounds (light-pillar, ralayoḥ prakāśastambhasvabhāvatvāt), unmanifest (else creation, not will); four neuters ṛṝḷḹ bearing both shadows.

## tsa03-p02
"When there is spreading of unsurpassed-and-bliss into wills, then the phoneme-pair e, oṃ. There again, from regrouping of unsurpassed-and-bliss, the pair ai, au. That is action-power, and that four — e, ai, o, au. Then again, at the end of action-power, all effect-things about to enter the unsurpassed rest first as sensation-essence, as light-alone, as bindu: am. Then therein arises the emission of the unsurpassed: aḥ. Thus the sixteen of graspings is called seed-natured. Risen thence, consonant-natured, womb-natured. Therein, from unsurpassed the ka-class; of faith, from will the ca-class; of action-willed will, the two ṭa and ta classes; from unfolding the pa-class; by five-power yoga, fivefoldness. Of threefold will alone: ya, ra, la; from unfolding, va; of threefold will alone: śa, ṣa, sa; from emission, ha; womb-union-born, kṣa. Thus indeed this Lord, unsurpassed, is Kuleśvara-form. Of him there is one kaulikī emission-power, by which, from bliss-nature onward to outer-creation-end, throbbing, the class-and-graspings become outer tattva-natured. And this emission is threefold: āṇava of mind-rest-nature, śākta of mind-awakening-mark, śāmbhava of mind-dissolution-nature. Thus emission itself, in world-making, is the Lord's power. Thus when grasping is undividedly, then the one Lord alone, as seed-womb; in part-grasping, possessor-of-power and power. In separate eight-grasping, with wheel-lord-company, nine classes; with per-grasping primacy, fifty-natured. There too, in grasping possible part-division differences, eighty-one-natured. But really there are six graspings, becoming twelve through forth-and-back yoga, nourishing the Lord's power-fullness of the universe. They themselves, since grasping-natured, powers, goddesses, are etymologized as Śrī Kālīs. And these power-natured pure graspings, in pure knowledge, through parāpara-nature, through slight Māyā-unfolding-contraction, take vidyā-avidyā-lord-nature. In Māyā again, with manifest difference-divisions, they take Māyā-letter-nature — attaining usability in paśyantī, madhyamā, vaikharī, up to outer-form-tattva-nature-becoming. And they, though Māyā-made, when seen as body-scheme, and when by the stated means their revivification is done by the life-standing pure graspings, then become potent; and so disposed, they give enjoyment and liberation. Thus seeing the self, of mere all-grasping-rest-nature, with reflected all-tattva-being-world-divisions, thought-freely, by śāmbhava immersion — living liberation. Here too, as before, there is no mantra-constraint at all. (3.14–3.34)"

## tsa03-p02 — how the alphabet falls out of the graspings
When Unsurpassed and Bliss pour into the wills, two letters sound: e, oṃ. Clashing back together, two more: ai, au — and that foursome is action-power itself. When every effect is about to rest back in the Unsurpassed, it waits first as pure sensing, sheer light, a point: aṃ. Then, right there, the Unsurpassed breathes out: aḥ. Sixteen graspings, all seed. Out of seed, the consonants, the womb. From the Unsurpassed, the k-row; from will-as-faith, the c-row; from action-joined will, the two ṭ- and t-rows; from unfolding, the p-row — five by yoga with the five powers. From threefold will alone: y, r, l; from unfolding, v; from threefold will: ś, ṣ, s; from emission, h; from womb's union, kṣa. So the Lord, unsurpassed, wears Kuleśvara's shape. His is one clan-emission-power: from bliss-nature throbbing all the way out to creation's edge, graspings turn into outer principles. The emission is three: stopping mind (atom's way), waking mind (power's way), dissolving mind (Śambhu's way) — emission itself is how the Lord worlds the world. Grasped whole, he is one, seed-and-womb; grasped in parts, owner and owned. Eight graspings apart, with their wheel-lords: nine clans. One grasping leading: fifty. Dividing further: eighty-one. But truly six graspings, twelve going and returning, keep the Lord full of the universe's powers — and as powers, those goddesses spell Kālī. Pure graspings, in pure knowing, take a half-other shape and narrow slightly with Māyā's dawn into lords of knowing and unknowing. In Māyā they splinter openly into Māyā-letters, usable through seeing, middle, and outer speech down to outer principles. Read as the body's plan and re-ensouled by the pure graspings that outlive them, even fallen letters turn potent — giving pleasure and freedom both. Who sees the self this way — nothing but rest in all graspings, with every principle, being, and world mirrored in it — thought-free, in Śambhu's immersion, is free while living. And here too: no mantra strings attached.
